findings.claim: The cast check for IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver never matches an explicit interface implementation. Roslyn names an explicit implementation with its interface prefix, for example "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize", so `m.Name == "OnBeforeSerialize"` is never true. The check also only looks at `type.GetMembers()`, so explicit implementations on a base class are missed. As a result needsCast is always false. For a type that implements the callbacks explicitly, the template emits `value.OnBeforeSerialize()`, and the generated formatter fails to compile with CS1061.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCallbackReceiverTests.ExplicitCallbackReceiverImplementationCompiles. It declares a class that implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver explicitly, plus a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial formatter for it. Expect it to fail on head with an unexpected CS1061 in the generated formatter source.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored. Without a surrogate, CreateContractlessMembers always serializes every public read-write member under its name as a string key, even when T carries [MessagePackObject] with [Key(int)] and [IgnoreMember]. A T annotated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] therefore gets a map-format formatter instead of an array-format one, and [IgnoreMember] members are still serialized. The requirement says attributes on T must be honoured, and L19 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Build a referenced assembly containing `[MessagePackObject] public class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int B {get;set;} }`. Then run the generator on a compilation with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {}`. Assert the generated F source contains `WriteArrayHeader` and does not reference `B`. On head it uses WriteMapHeader and serializes B.

findings.claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration, but the formatter body is emitted inside EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces using the user formatter's real containing types (Formatter = new QualifiedNamedTypeName(formatter)). A formatter nested in a non-partial class, such as `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<X> {} }`, gets no MsgPack019. The generated code redeclares `partial class Outer`, which produces CS0260 (missing partial modifier) instead of a clear diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run VerifyCS with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck on source with a non-partial `class Outer` containing `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject> {}` and a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver]. Expect CS0260 from the generated file and no MsgPack019.

findings.claim: The surrogate is read with `.Value.Value as INamedTypeSymbol`. A SurrogateType that is not a named type, for example `typeof(Surrogate[])`, or an erroneous type therefore becomes null, and the formatter silently falls back to contractless mode with no diagnostic. The user's intended key contract is dropped without any error.

receipt_plan.detail: Declare `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(S[]))] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject> {}` where S has [Key(0)] members. Assert that a diagnostic is reported. On head, no diagnostic is reported and a string-keyed contractless formatter is generated.
